fields.options: For whoever runs the library: its name and look, the languages and order of the portal, and its address. Settings by kind of library

fields.label: Portal Title
fields.description: The library's name on the portal, in the browser tab, in the Desk and in citations.

fields.label: Tagline
fields.default: Find, read and cite digitised books from Servants of Knowledge and the Internet Archive.
fields.description: One line under the name on the portal home page.

fields.label: Public Base URL
fields.description: e.g. https://library.example.org. Used in citations, OAI-PMH and MARC 856 links. Leave empty to use this site's URL.

fields.label: OAI Repository Identifier
fields.description: Domain-style identifier used in OAI identifiers, e.g. library.example.org

fields.label: Admin Email
fields.options: Email
fields.description: Shown to OAI-PMH harvesters.

fields.label: Portal Languages
fields.description: Languages the portal is offered in besides English, one code a line (kn for Kannada, hi Hindi, ta Tamil, te Telugu, ml Malayalam, mr Marathi, sa Sanskrit…). Readers get a language switch at the top of the portal; translate the portal's words in Portal Translations.

fields.label: Default Order
fields.options:
Oldest first
Newest first
Title A–Z
Relevance
fields.description: How books are listed on the portal (the library, collections, search) until a reader chooses another order in the Sort menu. Books without a year come last.

fields.label: Best Matches First When Searching
fields.description: When a reader types words to search, show the best matches first instead of the default order (they can still choose Oldest first).

fields.label: Logo
fields.description: PNG, SVG or JPG. Shown on the portal home page, in the top bar of every portal page and in the Desk. A wide logo about 400×120 px works well; add a square Icon below for the Desk's small icons.

fields.label: Show Logo on the Home Page
fields.description: Show the logo above the name on the portal home page.

fields.label: Show Portal Name Next to the Logo in the Top Bar
fields.description: Turn off when the logo already contains the library's name.

fields.label: Icon (optional)
fields.description: Square image (PNG/ICO/SVG, 64×64 or larger): the browser tab and the Research Desk icon in the Desk. Leave empty to use the logo.

fields.label: Home Page Background Image (optional)
fields.description: A wide photo behind the search box on the home page, e.g. a manuscript or library shelf.

fields.label: Your Institution
fields.description: Tick every kind of institution this library is; they combine. Ticking or unticking one sets the features below to what the ticked ones need, and the resource preset to the largest of theirs. You can still change each feature afterwards.

fields.label: Small library or school
fields.description: Switches on: OCR, books from folders and servers. Resources: light.

fields.label: Public research portal
fields.description: Switches on: page-level full-text search, OCR, proofreading and ground truth, readers' notes, authority control, review queue, permanent identifiers, sharing metadata, usage statistics. Resources: standard.

fields.label: Members-only institution
fields.description: Switches on: page-level full-text search, reader accounts, library systems, review queue, sharing metadata. Resources: standard.

fields.label: Archive keeping its own copies
fields.description: Switches on: preservation, permanent identifiers, books from folders and servers, review queue. Resources: standard.

fields.label: University or repository front
fields.description: Switches on: page-level full-text search, OCR, books from repositories, books from folders and servers, permanent identifiers, sharing metadata, library systems. Resources: standard.

fields.label: Language-technology partner
fields.description: Switches on: page-level full-text search, OCR, proofreading and ground truth, sharing metadata. Resources: server.

fields.label: Features
fields.description: A feature that is off is not collected: its scheduled work stops, its Desk screens go and nothing new of its kind is made. What exists stays, and who sees it is still decided by access (roles and each book's visibility). The catalogue, archive.org, book search, the reader, collections, citations and the Server page are always on.

fields.label: Page-level full-text search
fields.description: Search inside the text of every page, page hits, search inside a book. Off saves most of the search engine's disk, memory and CPU.

fields.label: OCR
fields.description: Reading scans with OCR, re-OCR of pages and books. Off saves CPU (OCR is the heaviest work Research Desk does).

fields.label: Proofreading and ground truth
fields.description: Correcting and validating page text, sharing corrected pages as OCR ground truth. Off saves worker time and a portal section.

fields.label: Readers' notes
fields.description: Highlights, comments, tags and OCR error reports; research groups. Off saves review work for managers.

fields.label: Authority control
fields.description: Authors and subjects matched to Wikidata, VIAF and LCSH, and giving back to them. Off saves nightly jobs and calls to outside services.

fields.label: Review queue
fields.description: Records checked for what needs a cataloguer (no year, wrong language, duplicates). Off saves nightly checks.

fields.label: Preservation
fields.description: The library's own checked copies (OCFL), fixity, a second copy, BagIt exports. Off saves disk (often as much as the collection itself) and nightly audits.

fields.label: Permanent identifiers
fields.description: ARKs for books and pages, DOIs from DataCite, tombstones. Off saves little; its screens and the DataCite calls.

fields.label: Books from folders and servers
fields.description: IA-style book folders and loose PDFs on disk, a NAS or a web server. Off saves the folder scans.

fields.label: Books from repositories
fields.description: DSpace, EPrints and any OAI-PMH repository. Off saves the harvests.

fields.label: Library systems
fields.description: A Koha or other library catalogue matched to the books here, links sent back. Off saves the imports and matching.

fields.label: Repository deposit
fields.description: People deposit their own work (files, licence, embargo) for a reviewer to accept. Off saves the deposit pages and the review screen.

fields.label: Sharing metadata
fields.description: The OAI-PMH provider, pushes to Koha, Wikidata, archive.org and webhooks. Off saves the push jobs and the OAI-PMH endpoint.

fields.label: Reader accounts
fields.description: Readers signing up, sign-up requests, members-only reading. Off saves the sign-up pages.

fields.label: Usage statistics
fields.description: How readers use the portal (built-in, PostHog, Plausible or Umami). Off saves the page-view log.

fields.options: Who can find and read what, how readers sign up, and how the portal's use is counted. Settings by kind of library

fields.label: Access & Sign-up
fields.description: Choose what visitors who are not logged in can do, and how people become readers. Logged-in readers and staff can always find and read every published book.

fields.label: Visitors Who Are Not Logged In
fields.options:
Each item's setting
Records only
Login required
fields.description: Each item's setting: follow each book's “Who can see it”. Records only: visitors can search the catalogue and cite, but reading and search inside the text need a login. Login required: the whole portal is for logged-in readers (an internal library).

fields.label: Default for New Books
fields.options:
Public
Login to read
Login to find
fields.description: Used when neither the ingest profile nor a rule below decides.

fields.label: Reader Accounts
fields.options:
Admins add readers
Anyone can sign up
Sign up, admin approves
fields.description: Admins add readers: no sign-up page; add people in User with the ResDesk Reader role, or ./resdesk.sh add-reader. Anyone can sign up: every account can read. Sign up, admin approves: new accounts wait in Reader Requests.

fields.label: OAI-PMH Shares
fields.options:
Records guests can find
All published records
Off
fields.description: What harvesters such as Koha receive. “All published records” suits a library system on an internal network.

fields.label: Access Rules
fields.description: Set visibility of new books by collection, subject, language, author, source or ingest profile. The first matching rule wins; an ingest profile's own “Access for Its Books” comes first. Use “Apply Access Rules” to update books already in the catalogue.

fields.label: Rules
fields.options: RD Access Rule
fields.description: Give books a visibility by collection, subject, language, creator, source or profile. Press Apply Access Rules to use them on books already in the catalogue.

fields.label: The Desk
fields.description: Staff work in Research Desk; Frappe's own tools (Build, Users, Website, Integrations…) are hidden from the Desk's sidebar, app screen and search. Roles still decide what each person may open. The Administrator account always sees everything.

fields.label: What Staff See in the Desk
fields.options:
Research Desk only, except Administrator
Research Desk only for staff; System Managers see everything
Everything (Frappe's own tools too)
fields.description: Applies to everyone with a ResDesk staff role or System Manager. Changing it updates every account straight away.

fields.label: Usage Statistics
fields.description: How readers use the portal: pages seen, searches, books opened. Only the portal is counted, never the Desk; no cookies and no personal data are sent.

fields.label: Statistics
fields.options:
Off
Built-in
PostHog
Plausible
Umami
fields.description: Built-in: counted on this server (Frappe's page views), shown on the Research Desk dashboard; nothing leaves the server. PostHog, Plausible or Umami: sent to that service (cloud or your own), with its own dashboards.

fields.label: Service address
fields.description: PostHog: https://us.i.posthog.com, https://eu.i.posthog.com or your own. Plausible: https://plausible.io or your own. Umami: your Umami server, or https://cloud.umami.is.

fields.label: Project key or site id
fields.description: PostHog: the project API key (phc_…). Plausible: the site's domain as added there. Umami: the website id.

fields.label: Dashboard link
fields.options: URL
fields.description: Optional: where staff open the statistics (shown on the Research Desk dashboard).

fields.options: For cataloguers: bringing books in from archive.org, collections kept in step with it, and matching authors and subjects to authorities. Settings by kind of library

fields.label: Contact (sent in User-Agent)
fields.description: An email or URL so IA can reach you if your harvesting causes problems.

fields.label: Delay Between Requests (seconds)
fields.description: Pause between requests to archive.org. Raise it if archive.org asks you to slow down.

fields.label: Books per Background Batch
fields.description: Large ingests are split into batches that run in parallel, one per queue worker. Add workers with QUEUE_WORKERS in .env.

fields.label: Keep a Local Copy of Page Text
fields.description: Stores compressed OCR text on disk (about 20–60 KB per book) so re-indexing never needs to download from archive.org again.

fields.label: Pause Scheduled Ingests
fields.description: Stops Hourly/Daily/Weekly profiles and the daily sync with archive.org from starting new runs. Manual runs still work. Also on the Background Jobs page.

fields.label: Pause All Background Work
fields.description: Set from the Background Jobs page: runs are paused and queued jobs held until you press Resume All there.

fields.label: Collections from archive.org
fields.description: Portal collections that mirror archive.org: made and kept up to date by themselves as books come in, change or leave.

fields.label: A Portal Collection for Every archive.org Collection
fields.description: Every archive.org collection your books belong to (such as the Servants of Knowledge sub-collections) gets its own collection page on the portal, named after it, with its description, shown under the collection it belongs to. Off: only the collection of each ingest profile that asks for one.

fields.label: Smallest Collection to Show
fields.description: Only make a page for archive.org collections with at least this many of your books.

fields.label: Skip These archive.org Collections
fields.description: archive.org collection identifiers that should not get a page, one per line (for example a big general collection most of your books are also in).

fields.label: Read Scans with OCR
fields.description: Books whose PDF has no text (scans from a repository or your folders) are read with Tesseract in the background, in the book's languages, so they can be searched inside and proofread. Needs Tesseract and its language models (Server → Requirements). Books on archive.org already come with their text.

fields.label: Space for Downloaded PDFs (GB)
fields.description: PDFs fetched from repositories and book servers to draw their pages (for OCR, proofreading and Page & text) are kept here up to this size; the least used go first.

fields.label: Find Authority Matches Nightly
fields.description: Each night, look up 300 more authors on Wikidata and 300 subjects in the Library of Congress Subject Headings, and propose matches on Desk → Authorities (the names with most books first).

fields.label: Accept Near-Certain Matches
fields.description: Accept a match without a person when it is near-certain: one person on Wikidata with the same name, dates that fit the books, and no other candidate close. Everything else waits for a cataloguer.

fields.options: The search engine: where it runs, what is indexed, and search in Latin letters for Indian scripts. Settings by kind of library

fields.label: Meilisearch URL
fields.description: Where the search engine runs. The installer sets this; change it only if you move Meilisearch.

fields.label: Meilisearch API Key
fields.description: The key the installer created for the search engine. Keep it secret.

fields.label: Index Prefix
fields.description: Lets several sites share one Meilisearch.

fields.label: Index Page-Level Full Text
fields.description: Enables deep search inside books. Uses more disk.

fields.label: Find Indic Spellings
fields.description: A search typed in Latin letters (vachana, kanakadasa) also finds the words in the scripts of the catalogue's languages (ವಚನ, ಕನಕದಾಸ), using the spellings the catalogue really holds.

fields.label: Max Characters per Page
fields.description: Longer pages are cut to this length in the index, which keeps it smaller.

fields.label: Search Status
fields.description: Filled in by Test Search Engine: whether it connected and how many books and pages the index holds.

fields.options: For partners and researchers: permanent ARKs, DOIs from DataCite, and the corrected pages shared as OCR ground truth. Settings by kind of library

fields.label: Give Books ARKs
fields.description: Switch on when the ARK Alliance has given the library its NAAN (free: arks.org → Request a NAAN). Every book then gets a permanent ARK (the ones already here in the background), shown as Permanent link and used in citations, exports and OAI-PMH; the portal answers <portal>/ark:/… itself. Once on, the NAAN and shoulder can't be changed.

fields.label: ARK NAAN
fields.description: The number the ARK Alliance gave this library (five or more digits). Needed before Give Books ARKs can be switched on; 99999, the Alliance's test number, is not accepted.

fields.label: ARK Shoulder
fields.description: The prefix of the books' ARK names: letters then one digit (b1 for books). Fixed once ARKs are switched on.

fields.label: DOIs (DataCite)
fields.description: For libraries that are DataCite members (directly or through a consortium): the books of collections marked Give DOIs get a DOI pointing at their page on the portal.

fields.label: Give DOIs
fields.description: Register DOIs for the books of collections marked Give DOIs, every night and from a collection's form.

fields.label: DataCite Test System
fields.description: Use DataCite's test system (api.test.datacite.org) while trying this out: its DOIs never resolve and never show in citations. Untick once the library's production account is ready.

fields.label: DOI Prefix
fields.description: The prefix DataCite gave the library, e.g. 10.12345.

fields.label: DataCite Repository ID
fields.description: The repository's ID in DataCite Fabrica, e.g. SOK.LIBRARY.

fields.label: DataCite Repository Password
fields.description: The repository's password in DataCite Fabrica. Kept encrypted.

fields.label: DOI Shoulder
fields.description: Put before each book's identifier in its DOI: 10.12345/rd.kanakadasa1950. Never change it once DOIs are given.

fields.label: Ground Truth
fields.description: Proofread pages with their images, shared as an open set for training and testing OCR (Ground Truth in the Desk).

fields.label: Licence for Ground Truth
fields.options:
CC0-1.0
CC-BY-4.0
CC-BY-SA-4.0
fields.description: Under which licence the library shares its corrected texts. Until one is chosen, sets are made for the library's own use only and none can be put on the portal. CC0: no conditions; CC-BY: credit; CC-BY-SA: credit and share alike.

fields.label: Credit Line
fields.description: How reusers should credit the set, e.g. Servants of Knowledge and its volunteer proofreaders.

fields.label: Name the Proofreaders
fields.description: Put each page's proofreader and validator (their full names, never their emails) in the set's manifest. Ask them first.

fields.options: For archivists: the library's own checked copies of the books, and a second copy elsewhere. Settings by kind of library

fields.label: Preservation Folder
fields.description: Where the library's own copies of its books are kept (a disk or NAS folder the server can write to, e.g. /preservation in Docker). Empty: no copies are kept. Each book is stored as an OCFL object: plain files and a checksum inventory any future system can read.

fields.label: Preserve
fields.options:
Off
Books in collections marked Preserve
Every book
fields.description: Which books get a copy. Copies are made a few hundred a night (Background Jobs shows them); a book ingested again gets a new version only if a file changed.

fields.label: Include Page Images
fields.description: Also keep the original scans from archive.org, not only the PDF, OCR and metadata. Much larger (often 10-50 times), but the copy is then complete enough to make new OCR from.

fields.label: Space for Copies (GB)
fields.description: The most the copies may take. 0: as much as the disk allows (the last 5% of the disk is never used).

fields.label: Check Every (days)
fields.description: Every copy is checked against its checksums at least this often: each night a share of them is checked. A copy that fails is marked and alerts on the Server page.

fields.label: Second Copy
fields.description: A second copy of every preserved book, somewhere else: another disk, a NAS, a partner's storage mounted on this server, or an S3-compatible bucket. Each copy is checked on the same schedule; when one fails its check and the other is good, the bad one is rebuilt from the good one.

fields.label: Second Copy
fields.options:
Off
Folder
S3-compatible
fields.description: Folder: another disk, a NAS or a partner's storage mounted on this server. S3-compatible: a bucket on Amazon S3, Wasabi, Backblaze B2, MinIO or similar.

fields.label: Second Copy Folder
fields.description: On another disk or a mounted share, not inside the first copy's folder, e.g. /mnt/nas/sok-copies.

fields.label: S3 Endpoint
fields.description: The service's address, e.g. https://s3.eu-central-1.wasabisys.com, https://s3.us-west-004.backblazeb2.com or a partner's MinIO. Empty for Amazon S3.

fields.label: S3 Region
fields.description: The bucket's region, e.g. eu-central-1 (some services need it, others ignore it).

fields.label: S3 Bucket
fields.description: The bucket's name; make it first, on the service, and keep it private.

fields.label: Folder in the Bucket
fields.description: Optional, e.g. sok-library.

fields.label: S3 Access Key
fields.description: A key with read, write, list and delete rights on this bucket only.

fields.label: S3 Secret Key
fields.description: Stored encrypted; never shown again after saving.

fields.label: Keep Dropped Books on the Portal
fields.description: When archive.org stops serving a book we hold a copy of, keep it on the portal and serve its PDF from our copy instead of taking it down. archive.org often darkens books for rights reasons: leave this off to decide book by book (book form → Serve From Our Copy).

fields.options: For whoever runs the machine: workers and other resources, quiet hours, updates, backups and alerts. Settings by kind of library

fields.label: Resource Preset
fields.options:
light
standard
server
fields.description: How much of the machine Research Desk may use: light (a laptop), standard, or server (a dedicated machine). Docker's limits can only be changed outside the app, so after choosing, run ./resdesk.sh resources apply on the server.

fields.label: Parallel Workers
fields.description: How many background jobs run at once: ingest batches and first-pass parts, so how many books come in together (1 to 16; 4 to 6 stay polite to archive.org when page text is fetched). Saving applies it through the updater helper; without the helper, the Desk shows the command to run. Empty: as set on the server.

fields.label: Largest Upload (MB)
fields.description: The largest file people can upload in the Desk: metadata files for ingest, spreadsheets, attachments (1 to 1000).

fields.label: Worker Priority
fields.description: How much CPU the background workers get compared with the portal, search and database: 19 is the lowest (they only use what the others leave), 0 the same as the others, -5 ahead of them. Empty: as the workers were started (WORKER_NICE). Changed live from Background Jobs → Machine too: each worker takes it on when it starts its next book.

fields.label: Books First Automatically
fields.description: When a new book has waited more than 15 minutes in the search engine behind page text, do what Background Jobs → Search queue → Books first does: the waiting page text is cancelled and sent again later, so new books reach the portal first. At most every 30 minutes.

fields.label: Book Limit
fields.options:
Automatic
A number I choose
No limit
fields.description: How many books the catalogue may hold. Automatic: what this machine's CPUs, memory and disk can take (the Server page shows the numbers). At the limit, ingests keep updating books already here but add no new ones. Books with many pages count for more.

fields.label: Books at Most
fields.description: The limit in books of this library's average size (more than the machine can take is allowed, at your own risk).

fields.label: Quiet Hours
fields.description: Pause all background work between these times every day (e.g. office hours), and carry on afterwards. Ingests, pushes and re-indexing wait; the portal and Desk work as usual.

fields.label: Quiet From
fields.description: Start of the quiet time, in the site's time zone.

fields.label: Quiet Until
fields.description: End of the quiet time. Earlier than Quiet From means overnight (e.g. 22:00 to 06:00).

fields.label: Weekdays Only
fields.description: Monday to Friday only; weekends run freely.

fields.label: Server & Updates
fields.description: Updates, backups and alerts. The Server page (Research Desk → Server) shows the state of each part and, with the updater helper turned on, upgrades and restarts from the Desk.

fields.label: Check for New Releases
fields.description: Once a day, look on GitHub for a newer Research Desk release and Frappe patch, and tell managers when there is one.

fields.label: Allow Upgrades and Restarts from the Desk
fields.description: Only matters when the updater helper is turned on (./resdesk.sh updater on). Untick to allow them on the server only; the Server page still shows everything.

fields.label: Automatic Backups
fields.options:
Off
Daily
Weekly
fields.description: Back up the database every night (Weekly: on Sunday night). Backups are kept on the server; download them from the Server page and keep copies elsewhere.

fields.label: Include Uploaded Files
fields.description: Also back up uploaded files (logos, pictures, attachments). Books themselves are never in backups: they stay on archive.org or in your folders.

fields.label: Backups to Keep
fields.description: Older backups are deleted after each new one.

fields.label: Email Alerts to Managers
fields.description: When a part stops working, the disk is nearly full, a backup or upgrade fails, or a new release is out. Needs an outgoing email account (Desk → Email Account). Alerts always appear in the Desk's notifications too.

fields.label: Also Email
fields.description: More addresses for alerts, separated by commas.

fields.label: Alert Webhook URL
fields.options: URL
fields.description: Also post alerts as JSON to this address, for example a Slack, Mattermost or Discord incoming webhook (the text is in "text").

fields.label: Alert When Disk Is This Full (%)
fields.description: Warn when the disk holding Research Desk's data is this full.
